q: Which nutrient is the main body-building food?
e: Protein builds and repairs body cells.

q: Kwashiorkor is mainly caused by a lack of
e: Children who do not get enough protein develop kwashiorkor.

q: A lack of vitamin C in the diet causes
e: Scurvy shows as bleeding gums and slow healing of wounds.

q: Rickets in children is caused by a lack of vitamin
e: Vitamin D helps the body use calcium to make strong bones.

q: Which mineral salt prevents goitre?
e: A lack of iodine makes the thyroid gland swell, which is goitre.

q: Anaemia is mainly caused by a lack of
e: Iron is needed to make haemoglobin in the red blood cells.

q: Which of these foods is rich in carbohydrate?
e: Yam, cassava, rice and bread give energy as carbohydrate.

q: Beriberi is caused by a lack of vitamin
e: Thiamine is found in whole grains, beans and meat.

q: Which of these is a moist method of cooking?
e: Boiling, steaming and stewing cook food in water or steam.

q: Cooking food in hot fat or oil is called
e: Frying uses hot oil to cook and brown the food.

q: Cooking food gently in liquid just below boiling point is called
e: Simmering keeps the liquid barely bubbling.

q: Which of these is a raising agent used in baking?
e: Baking powder gives off gas that makes cakes rise.

q: Which of these is a natural fibre that comes from a plant?
e: Cotton comes from the cotton plant; the others are made in factories.

q: Which of these is a natural fibre from an animal?
e: Wool comes from the fleece of sheep.

q: Which of these is a synthetic fibre?
e: Nylon is made from chemicals.

q: The tool used to take body measurements for a garment is the
e: A tape measure bends round the body, so it measures chest, waist and hips.

q: The part of a sewing machine that holds the fabric down while sewing is the
e: The presser foot keeps the cloth flat against the feed dog.

q: Soap is made from fats or oils and
e: Fat or oil reacts with an alkali such as caustic soda to make soap.

q: A family budget is a plan that compares
e: A budget shows the money coming in and how it will be spent.

q: Which of these is a fixed expense for a family?
e: Rent stays the same each month, so it is fixed.

q: A family made up of a father, a mother and their children is called a
e: A nuclear family has only parents and children.

q: An extended family includes the parents, children and also
e: It stretches beyond parents and children to other relatives.

q: A balanced diet is one that contains
o: all the classes of food in the right amounts
a lot of fat and sugar
e: It supplies all nutrients in the amounts the body needs.

q: Drying is a method of food preservation because it
o: removes the water that micro-organisms need
e: Without water, bacteria and moulds cannot grow.

q: Keeping food in a refrigerator helps to
e: Cold slows down spoilage but does not stop it completely.

q: Food poisoning is commonly caused by
e: Bacteria such as Salmonella grow in badly handled food.

q: Which of these insects spreads cholera and typhoid by touching food?
e: Houseflies carry germs from dirt onto food.

q: Which of these foods is a good source of vitamin A?
e: Carrots and palm oil contain carotene, which the body turns into vitamin A.

q: Roughage in the diet helps to prevent
e: Fibre helps food move through the bowel.

q: Which nutrient gives the most energy per gram?
e: Fat gives about 9 kilocalories a gram; carbohydrate and protein give about 4.

q: Fruits and vegetables are called protective foods because they
o: supply vitamins and minerals that protect the body from disease
e: Vitamins and minerals protect against deficiency diseases.

q: A pressure cooker is useful because it
o: cooks food faster and saves fuel
e: Steam under pressure raises the cooking temperature.

q: In weaving, the warp threads run
e: The weft threads cross the warp from side to side.

q: The selvedge of a fabric is
e: It runs down both lengthwise edges and does not fray.

q: A paper pattern in dressmaking is used as
o: a guide for cutting out the garment
e: The pieces are pinned to the cloth and cut round.

q: Starch is used in laundry work to
o: make fabrics stiff and keep them clean longer
e: Starch gives collars and uniforms a crisp finish.

q: A consumer is a person who
o: buys and uses goods and services
e: Consumers use the goods and services that producers supply.

q: In Nigeria, the agency that regulates food, drugs and packaged water is
e: NAFDAC protects consumers by checking the quality of food and drugs.

q: Using family resources wisely to reach family goals is called
e: It means planning, organising and controlling resources such as time, money and energy.
